title: AI arXiv daily — 8 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-paper ordering based on visible cross-listing, evaluation scope, artifacts, and limited external discovery signals—not readership or download counts. These papers are under a day old at snapshot time, so citation evidence is sparse.

sections.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
sections.abstract: Trains a JEPA latent world model on data from 12 robot embodiments and reports power-law scaling of latent rollout error with compute, correlated with downstream planning performance, including zero-shot real-robot tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say this is the first scaling-law study for multi-embodiment robotic world models trained on real-robot data, and that latent imagination error can serve as a proxy for planning performance.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not establish that its scaling relation or proxy remains reliable for other robot datasets, tasks, or model families.

sections.title: SciExam for ENSO: Can AI Agents Build Climate Models?
sections.abstract: Introduces a benchmark where agents build stochastic ENSO climate models from observations under a six-hour budget; six of twelve evaluated systems reportedly score above a published model on hidden statistical, reconstruction, and forecasting tests.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors present SciExam as a way to assess agent-generated scientific models without a known single answer, and report competitive models whose simplified structures align with one of two live ENSO explanations.
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence is for one climate phenomenon and a twelve-system comparison; it does not establish general scientific-discovery ability.

sections.title: RECAST: Learning to Compute the Right Context through Adaptive Evidence Routing
sections.abstract: Treats evidence construction as sequential routing across retrieval and computation tools; its learned router reportedly reaches 75.6% mean success across six benchmark families and improves on the strongest large-model baseline by 15.9%.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors' RECAST system uses a learned RouterLM to select or formulate retrieval/computation operations, then passes accepted evidence to a separate answer model; they report a 15.0% average gain on held-out benchmarks.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported generalization is limited to the stated held-out benchmark set; the abstract does not establish performance on unrestricted real-world evidence workflows.

sections.title: RobotWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Robot Use Across Diverse Tasks and Embodiments
sections.abstract: Presents an 84-task simulation testbed for multimodal agents using robot interfaces and finds that agents can build perception/control workflows but often fail to preserve task state, recover from ineffective actions, or recognize completion.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide an execution-trace benchmark and diagnose capability-composition gaps rather than scoring only final outcomes.
sections.unique_caveat: This is explicitly a simulation testbed; success in simulation does not establish reliable deployment on physical robots.

sections.title: Decoupling Exploration from Optimization in RLVR
sections.abstract: Proposes Exploration-Distillation (ExpDis), which explores with novelty bonuses, filters useful trajectories, and distills them into a separate student; it reports improvements over DAPO at equal wall-clock budget on seven math benchmarks and two model families.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that separating high-novelty exploration from student optimization enables more aggressive exploration without the quality degradation they associate with novelty incentives applied directly to the student.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported evidence covers mathematical reasoning and two model families; the abstract does not establish that the method transfers to broader tasks or training setups.

sections.title: Before They Can Solve: Predicting Post-Training Coding-Agent Performance from Base Models
sections.abstract: Builds three trajectory-based screens for estimating a base model's potential as a coding agent; across ten public base/post-trained model pairs, the screens reportedly rank models in close agreement with post-trained SWE-bench Verified performance.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors use successful post-training trajectories and verifier-identified decisive actions to evaluate base checkpoints without requiring each checkpoint to cold-start and drive a full coding harness.
sections.unique_caveat: This method depends on successful benchmark trajectories and a verifier, and the reported validation is tied to SWE-bench Verified and ten model pairs.

sections.title: Open-MMUnlearning: Unifying Methods and Evaluation for MLLM Unlearning
sections.abstract: Releases an extensible multimodal-model unlearning framework spanning five privacy, safety, and copyright benchmarks, eight models, and twelve methods, and tests both method scores and the reliability of unlearning metrics.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors find that different metrics capture different properties: BLEU has the highest aggregate reliability, while KS-Test has the highest faithfulness AUC but weaker robustness.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract reports a finite set of eight models and five benchmarks; rankings among metrics and methods may change under other models, threat models, or data.

sections.title: RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs
sections.abstract: Adds an environment-side task record tracking requirements, read-file excerpts, provenance, and unopened candidates; the authors report consistent gains over plain workspace interaction and model-held records on three benchmarks and three LLMs.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors store task obligations and evidence in the environment, including a finish check for unresolved requirements, rather than relying on model memory alone.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract establishes results only for three benchmarks and three LLMs; broader workflow and file-corpus coverage remains untested in the reported summary.

sections.title: Reasoning-Token Spikes Under Prompted Untruthful Responding in Large Language Models
sections.abstract: In tests of three reasoning-capable models on 210 questions, truth-directed responses used fewer reasoning tokens on average than explicitly prompted false or truth-indifferent responses.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose reasoning-token count as a low-bandwidth candidate signal when chain-of-thought content is unavailable or unreliable.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly say this is not yet a detector of spontaneous deception or general misalignment; instance-level detection, generalization, and adversarial robustness remain untested.

method.ranking_note: Inferred notable-paper order based on cross-listing, external discovery, artifacts, and reported evaluation specificity; not readership/download counts.
method.limitations: Recent category pages checked for all core categories but not exhaustively across all entries; broad arXiv API query timed out. Semantic Scholar citation fields could not be verified at snapshot time.
